text:
Maya: Trying to collect an nsys trace from the dedicated-runner pod and hitting permission denied when nsys tries to write /tmp/trace.nsys. anyone seen this in k8s with nvidia-toolkit?
Sam: what exact error? can you paste the command + stderr?
Maya: here: `nsys profile --output /tmp/trace --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt`
Maya: returns: `ERROR: Could not open output file '/tmp/trace.nsys': Permission denied`
Jess: pretty common when the container process isn't allowed to write to the mounted dir. in our k8s jobs we mount an emptyDir at /tmp but the app runs as UID 1000 so /tmp is root owned.
Arjun: also be aware nsys creates shared mem/lock files; it may try to create under /tmp with different permissions.
Sam: can you run `ls -ld /tmp` and `id` inside the pod?
Maya: `drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 40 Mar 12 10:00 /tmp` and `uid=1000(redwood) gid=1000(redwood)`
Jess: quick fix is an initContainer that chowns the volume to the app uid. cheaper than running as root. example we use in other traces:
```
initContainers:
- name: fix-perms
  image: busybox
  command: ["sh","-c","chown -R 1000:1000 /nsys"]
  volumeMounts:
  - name: nsys-out
    mountPath: /nsys
volumes:
- name: nsys-out
  emptyDir: {}
containers:
- name: app
  volumeMounts:
  - name: nsys-out
    mountPath: /nsys
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 1000
```
Jess: then run `nsys profile --output /nsys/trace` from the app. avoids changing pod securityContext.
Maya: ok will try. thanks.
Arjun: unrelated but FYI our last perf run (nvprof+nsys) surfaces a perf regression: attention kernel selection is falling back to the generic matmul-based path for many sequences. timeline shows many small kernel launches and big memcpy around KV cache updates.
Sam: do you have the callchain/timeline screenshot or the nsys report snippet?
Arjun: pasted excerpt from the timeline: `flash_attn_fwd_fast` is attempted but immediately followed by `matmul_attention_fallback` for ~60% of tokens. the kernel time distribution is ~72% attention fallback, 18% memcpy, 10% others.
Arjun: probe indicates batching heuristic is grouping by arrival time rather than sequence length, resulting in mixed seq_len batches that force fallback kernel selection.
Maya: that explains the memcpy spikes — when batches mix short+long sequence we end up materializing KV caches and reformatting tensors on the host.
Sam: sounds like a kernel selection bug in the runtime: we should prefer grouping by max_seq_len or use per-bucket queues.
Jess: also check that the container isn't using an older cuBLAS/cuDNN; nvtx markers from the app looked different across nodes. container image must use the distro libs provided by nvidia-container-toolkit (no vendored drivers). mismatch can force software fallback kernels.
Maya: we saw two nodes with different driver versions in the nsys meta. one had `CUDA 12.1 driver 535.x`, other `CUDA 12.1 driver 520.x`.
Sam: that will cause behavior diffs for kernel selection. we need a runtime check that prints driver+lib versions at start and blocks rollout for mismatches.
Arjun: for KV cache behavior: the trace shows repeated GPU->CPU copies at start of generation for every request. looks like cache isn't being retained across worker processes; each worker reconstructs KV from model state and does a memcpy.
Sam: are we using shared GPU buffers or separate CUDA contexts per worker?
Arjun: separate contexts now. switching to a shared CUDA IPC handle (or using a single pinned worker that owns the cache) reduced copy count drastically in local repros.
Maya: ok plan: 1) patch k8s job template to include initContainer chown and mount path /nsys for traces, 2) add runtime guard to assert driver+lib compat at startup, 3) adjust batching heuristic to bucket by seq_len and prefer kernels flagged as fast, 4) prototype shared-KV cache via CUDA IPC and measure.
Jess: for collecting traces in k8s without privileged: prefer `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` + `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` for the trace container if you can't run as root. full privileged isn't necessary if you only need ptrace and perf_event syscalls. example docker testing command we used:
```
docker run --gpus all --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -v /tmp/nsys:/nsys --user 1000:1000 my-image nsys profile --output /nsys/trace --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt
```
Sam: note: seccomp=unconfined is still heavy; better to ship a narrow seccomp profile that allows perf_event_open + ptrace.
Maya: thanks. I'll try initContainer + driver-check at the same time and re-run the nsys capture. if the attention fallback persists i'll attach the .qdrep and timeline.
Arjun: when you re-run, include `--trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx` so we only capture the generation window (lower noise). also add `--stop-on-exit true` to ensure the file is flushed before container exits.
Maya: noted. i'll open a small PR for the k8s initContainer and the runtime driver-check.
deploy-bot: rollback scheduled: invocations=1, target=staging, reason=\"hotspot-attention-regression\" :rotating_light:
Sam: thanks, keep the rollout paused until we have the kernel-selection fix in canary.
Maya: will update here with the qdrep link once I have a good capture. :thumbsup:
